title: The Count-Duke of Olivares to the Duke of Alba, Madrid, 22 August 1626 (lead 1273): Philip IV's general cipher A, read; key partial by our protocol

documents.shelfmark: Madrid, BNE MSS/10249 ('Papeles varios', Osuna; BDH bdh0000042230), ff. 13r-15r (BNE Digital PDF pp. 16-18)
documents.route: Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares -> Antonio Álvarez de Toledo, 5th Duke of Alba (viceroy of Naples)

plaintext.source: No gloss, interlinear decipherment or key on ff. 13-15. A covering letter in clear of the same day (f. 11r) announces this one ('en otra carta que aquí le remito').

transcription.source: BNE Digital (Biblioteca Digital Hispánica) images at 120 dpi (not reproduced)

system.summary: Philip IV's general cipher 'A' (as used with the 2nd Marquis of Santa Cruz, 1629-1632): homophonic syllabary of letter groups (fer, xer, pon, tor ...), numbers for letters and syllables, special signs, and a nomenclator of numbers and groups for words (fro = Dios, 199 = hija, ber = servicio ...).
system.notes: The same general cipher as targets/santacruz1630 (1630), here already in use in August 1626. Diacritics: crosses/daggers above c and q, underlined signs (D_, C); a superscript '4' on a sign marks a null (as f4). Only the closing formula, the dateline and the signature are in clear.

prior_solution.where: DECODE R1190 lists this letter (BNE MSS/10249, Madrid 22 Aug 1626) with status 'Decrypted' and an inline-plaintext flag, behind authentication; its plaintext and key were not seen by us (your vetting note of 4 Nov 2026 on lead 1273 says the same). No edition found: Elliott & de la Peña, Memoriales y cartas del Conde Duque de Olivares (2013 ed.), table of contents: the only 1626 piece is doc. XI to the King; no letter to Alba. Nothing at Tomokiyo's or on the web.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the lead and set the rules (protocol hashed before any measurement, one measurement on a held-out part, no change to the measured key or transcription); he answered a blind pre-registered proof-reading of 13 sign forms (none from the held-out part) and decided, after the measurement, to read the three 'hol' of the held-out part by the value so established, counted as probable. AI agents transcribed, measured, read and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: ff. 13r-15r transcribed in the notation of key A (2,621 tokens); the held-out part H (f14v.21-27 + f15r, 542 tokens, 20.7%) only after the key was frozen.

Four neighbouring keys measured once each on the training part A: K6A (Santa Cruz 1630) reads it; K_OA1 = K6A + 20 values learnt on A by reading and from a fixed list of probable words; frozen by SHA-256.
One measurement on H: M5 0.506 against 0.144 for the best of 200 length-class shuffled keys; margin met, absolute threshold 0.60 missed (ceiling about 0.64 on a perfect plaintext of the series).

Blind, pre-registered proof-reading of 13 sign forms outside H by Brice Dudout (forms only, the sheet tested for leaks): hol = Su Majestad, gli = buena, 209 = 20 9, pr = for, nulls marked by a superscript 4.
Whole letter read by the sense after the measurement and counted by script by Daniel's rule: 1,001 words, 906 certain, 47 probable, 13 restored, 35 unresolved = 95.2%.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The general cipher A rebuilt from Santa Cruz pairs of 1630-32 (targets/santacruz1630, K6A) reads the training part of this letter; 20 values were added from that part only, then the key was frozen and measured once on the held-out part.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words not counted as read), counted by script on the marked reading (reading.md): 1,001 cipher words: 906 certain, 47 probable, 13 restored, 35 unresolved = 953/1,001 = 95.2%. About 54 line ends lost in the gutter (ff. 13v, 14v) are not counted. The three 'hol' of the held-out part are among the probable words (value established outside it).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py), one measurement: M5 (share of decoded letters covered by Spanish words of >= 5 letters) 0.506 on H (542 tokens) against 0.144 for the best of 200 keys shuffled within length classes (amendment written before H was transcribed). Criterion fixed in advance: >= 0.60 and >= best control + 0.30. Margin met (0.362), threshold not: partial by our protocol. M5 of a perfect contemporary plaintext of the same series is 0.636, so 0.60 asks for about 95% correctness.

credits.note: letter dated and identified (Olivares to Alba, 22 Aug 1626, with its covering letter in clear); cipher identified as Philip IV's general cipher A; key K6A extended (partial by our protocol: one held-out measurement 0.506 vs 0.144); letter transcribed, decrypted, read (95.2%) and translated. DECODE R1190 lists the letter as 'Decrypted' (plaintext not public, not seen): if that reading is earlier and complete, this credit should become 'verification'.

DECODE R1190 lists this letter with status 'Decrypted' and an inline-plaintext flag (record created 26 Aug 2019 with the DECODE Spanish series), behind authentication; its reading and key were not seen by us and not used

texts.label: Olivares to the Duke of Alba, Madrid, 22 August 1626 (BNE MSS/10249 ff. 13r-15r)
texts.summary: Olivares tells the Duke of Alba of his griefs of summer 1626: the death of a young Guzmán nephew meant for the Church; his daughter María's stillbirth, her recovery, then her death; her virtue. He keeps her widower Ramiro, Marquis of Toral, as son and heir of his house: the dukedom of Medina de las Torres on the commandery of Caravaca, the office of sumiller de corps given by the King of his own motion; he puts his life in the King's service and hopes the Duke his son will behave wisely.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 against translation.md: coherent Spanish of the 1620s from first to last line, a single family narrative. 1,001 words: 906 certain, 47 probable, 13 restored, 35 unresolved = 95.2%. Grade B: the key is partial by our protocol, 47 words rest on the sense or on a blind proof-reading of forms, and about 54 line ends are lost in the gutter, so ff. 13v and 14v read in fragments.
